CETA (EU–Canada Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement)
CPTPP (Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17 (PCMLTFA); Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46, s 462.31; Business Corporations Act, SBC 2002, c 57, Part 9.1 (Transparency Register of Significant Individuals), effective 1 May 2020; Business Corporations Act Regulation, BC Reg 30/2004; Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17; United Nations Act, RSC 1985, c U-2; FINTRAC Guidance and Interpretation Notice on beneficial ownership; FATF Recommendations 12, 22, 24 and 25.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access — the BC transparency register is maintained at the registered office and is not publicly searchable; disclosure is made to law enforcement and taxing authorities upon written request.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of Certificate of Incorporation of the ultimate foreign parent / holding company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or equivalent competent authority in the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization if the origin state is not a Hague member)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency (directors and officers) or Register of Members of the foreign parent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate service provider / registered agent maintaining the parent's statutory records

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent registry in the foreign parent's jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory CDD/EDD under PCMLTFA/FINTRAC: screen all directors, officers, shareholders ≥25% and UBOs against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, Global Affairs Canada's Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List (SEMA/UN Act), the FINTRAC entity sanctions list, and, given US payment rails (Apple IAP, Paymentwall), the OFAC SDN List and EU/UK consolidated lists as best practice. PEP screening follows FATF Rec. 12; source-of-funds and source-of-wealth verification required for any PEP or government-related UBO; adverse media and negative news checks are mandatory; screening reports are documented and retained for at least 5 years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BC Corporate Online (Registrar of Companies, British Columbia Registry Services, Ministry of Finance) — https://corporateonline.gov.bc.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Registered corporate names must be in Latin characters (English or French). Non-Latin script names (e.g., Chinese characters) cannot be used as the legal name; a transliteration or translation must be registered through a Name Request. The name must be distinct from all existing names in the NUANS corporate name database and must not be deceptively misdescriptive of the business, per BCBCA ss. 22–22.3.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Name Request is rejected, the applicant must (i) request a written statement of rejection grounds from the Corporate Registry Name Section via Corporate Online; (ii) file a reconsideration response with rebuttal evidence and supporting consents within 14 days; (iii) if rejected again, file a new Name Request where the objection is curable by distinctiveness, or file a petition for judicial review before the Supreme Court of British Columbia under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, RSBC 1996, c 241, within 60 days. The 56-day reservation may be renewed once for an additional 56 days.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible in form: BCBCA s. 52 requires a full street address in British Columbia, not a postal box; a 'virtual office' with a physical street address that can accept service of process is acceptable to the Registry. However, for a video-match/social app with fees processed through Apple IAP/Paymentwall, banks and payment providers will treat a virtual mailbox as heightened commercial-substance risk; the recommended structure is a physical law-firm/registered-agent address or a small leased suite, plus a local director/agent with access to corporate records and the transparency register.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (~10% in the first 12 months). BC Registrar inspections are complaint- and risk-driven; a low-risk, non-licensed internet application with a valid registered office and timely annual reports is unlikely to attract an unannounced site visit. FINTRAC compliance examination is not applicable unless the company later becomes a money services business or adds regulated financial activity.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: British Columbia Business Corporations Act, SBC 2002, c. 57 (BCBCA), Part 2 (Incorporation), ss. 9-14 (Incorporation Application, Notice of Articles, Notice of Directors, Certificate of Incorporation), ss. 101-102 (Registered Office and Records Office), ss. 30-33 (share issuance and consideration rules), ss. 141-144 (director appointment), ss. 266-274 (annual reporting and correction obligations)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: British Columbia Registrar of Companies, BC Corporate Registry, Ministry of Finance, Province of British Columbia
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Application (Form 1) accompanied by Notice of Articles (Form 1A) and Notice of Directors (Form 2), filed electronically through the BC Corporate Online portal
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum authorized or paid-up capital is prescribed under the BCBCA for incorporation; the incorporator may subscribe for one or more shares at any nominal issue price (e.g., CAD 0.01 per share). All issued shares must be fully paid under BCBCA s. 30 before a share certificate is delivered. If shares are issued for non-cash consideration, a written contract satisfying BCBCA s. 33 must be adopted and retained. No escrow account is required at the formation stage; escrow of promoter shares arises only if the corporation later becomes a reporting issuer under Canadian securities law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The undersigned, being the sole director of ___________ Corporation (the "Corporation"), acting by written resolution pursuant to the BCBCA, hereby resolves that: 1. The subscription of the incorporator for 5,000 Common Shares at CAD 0.01 per share is accepted, and such shares are issued fully paid and non-assessable. 2. The registered office and records office of the Corporation be established at _______________, British Columbia, subject to the consent of the office holder. 3. The following officers are appointed: ____________ as President and Chief Executive Officer, ____________ as Secretary, and ____________ as Chief Financial Officer, each to serve at the discretion of the board. 4. The directors adopt the Corporation's bylaws and fix the financial year-end as December 31.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation Name Availability Search and Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registrar of Companies via BC Corporate Online portal (https://corporateonline.gov.bc.ca)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a NUANS name search request through BC Corporate Online, selecting a distinct corporate name with a required legal element such as 'Inc.', 'Corp.', 'Ltd.' or 'Company'. Reserve the approved name for 56 days with the registrar. If a numbered company is preferred, no name reservation is necessary; the registrar will assign a sequential BC number followed by 'B.C. Ltd.'.
required_dossiers: Requested corporate name and legal element
Consent letter from any person whose name or trademark appears in the proposed name (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused as confusing or contrary to BCBCA Part 4, submit a revised name search with supporting consent letters, or apply for a numbered company designation; an aggrieved applicant may also seek registrarial reconsideration under the BCBCA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting Notice of Articles and Notice of Directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporators and the Corporation's legal advisors, British Columbia Corporate Registry form standards
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Notice of Articles (Form 1A) stating the corporate name, authorized share structure (e.g., one class of common shares, no par value), the number of directors, and the registered office and records office addresses in British Columbia. Prepare the Notice of Directors (Form 2) listing the first directors, their consent to act, and the statement that each is at least 18 years of age and not an undischarged bankrupt.
required_dossiers: Signed consent of each proposed director to act as director
Consent of registered office holder acknowledging the registered office and records office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar queries missing consents or incomplete share structure details, file supplementary consents and corrected forms electronically; the filing may be revised and resubmitted without additional incorporation fees if done before the certificate is issued.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registrar of Companies via BC Corporate Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into BC Corporate Online, select 'Incorporate a Company', upload or transcribe the Notice of Articles and Notice of Directors, and submit the Incorporation Application. Pay the CAD 350 statutory incorporation fee (approximately USD 260) by credit card or pre-authorized account. For paper filing, send the completed Form 1 package to the Registrar of Companies, PO Box 9431, Stn Prov Govt, Victoria, BC.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected or queried due to name conflict, fee error, or form defect, withdraw the application, correct the deficiency, and resubmit; the registrar's query letter will specify a cure period, and any erroneous certificate can be corrected through a registrar's correction request under the BCBCA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon acceptance, the registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation in electronic form, stating the company name, BC company number, and date of incorporation. Verify the certificate details and the 'Incorporation Date' on Corporate Online; the company exists as a legal entity from that date.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains an error, apply to the registrar within the prescribed period for a correction under the BCBCA; if the company was incorporated inadvertently, apply for administrative dissolution in accordance with the Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Meeting and First Board Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Corporation (internal governance)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first organizational board meeting or pass a unanimous written resolution covering: acceptance of the incorporator's share subscription (pro-forma First Board Resolution), adoption of bylaws, appointment of officers, approval of the registered office and records office, designation of the financial year-end, and selection of the corporate bank and authorized signatories.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director is unavailable to sign, the written resolution may be signed by all directors in counterparts; if the bylaws are not adopted at the first meeting, the statutory default bylaw provisions of the BCBCA apply pending later adoption.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Share Issuance and Statutory Records/Minute Book Preparation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Secretary and directors (internal records administration)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Issue share certificates to the subscribing shareholder in accordance with the board resolution, record the allotment in the share register, and maintain the statutory records at the British Columbia records office: the Notice of Articles, Notice of Directors, share register, directors' register, minutes, and consents. If shares are issued for non-cash consideration, retain the written contract required by BCBCA s. 33.
required_dossiers: Registered office and records office consent forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a statutory record is incomplete or lost, reconstruct the minute book by board resolution, obtain replacement consents, and file a register correction affidavit; the corporate registry will accept a formal declaration of record restoration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal and Provincial Tax Registration - CRA Business Number
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) through Business Registration Online (BRO)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the BRO registration at www.canada.ca/business-registration-online using the Certificate of Incorporation and BC company number. Obtain the 9-digit Business Number (BN) and the corporate income tax account (RC101), which covers both federal and British Columbia provincial corporate income tax under the federal-provincial collection agreement.
required_dossiers: Corporate information from Notice of Articles
Director identification and date of birth
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the BN is not activated promptly, call CRA Business Enquiries (1-800-959-5525) and provide the registry filing number; CRA will confirm the account activation date and backdate registration to the incorporation date if requested.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of GST/HST, Payroll, and Other Program Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and BC Ministry of Finance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Voluntarily register for a GST/HST account if the corporation expects revenue below CAD 30,000 to recover input tax credits; mandatory registration applies once taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 in a calendar quarter or four consecutive quarters. Register for payroll deductions (PD7A remittances) if employees are hired, and for import/export program accounts if international equipment or services are transacted. For the video-match app, ensure Apple IAP and Paymentwall proceeds are correctly characterized as electronic supplies for GST/HST purposes.
required_dossiers: CRA program account application (RC159 or BRO confirmation)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA queries the account activation or GST/HST registration date, respond within the requested period by providing incorporation date and commencement-of-business evidence such as the first board resolution and subscription agreement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Licence and Physical Office Occupancy Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local municipality business licensing office (e.g., City of Vancouver, Business Licence Office, if the office is in Vancouver) with fire department review
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a municipal business licence for 'Information Technology and Data Processing Services' at the physical office location. Provide evidence of zoning compliance for office use, the landlord's consent, and the Certificate of Incorporation. The local fire department will inspect the premises and issue an occupancy/fire safety clearance under the BC Fire Code and local by-laws.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the licence is refused on zoning grounds, obtain a city land-use declaration, apply for a minor variance or change-of-use permit, or relocate the registered office and re-apply; fire safety deficiencies can be remedied by installing required alarms/extinguishers and scheduling re-inspection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Environmental, WorkSafeBC, and Civil Defense Clearance for Physical Premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Environmental Assessment Office and BC Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy; WorkSafeBC; Technical Safety BC; local emergency management authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For a software data-processing and social telephony operation, obtain a written determination that the project is not a reviewable project under the BC Environmental Assessment Act (SBC 2018, c. 35) and that no waste discharge permit under the Environmental Management Act is required for domestic-only office sewage. Register the physical workplace with WorkSafeBC under the Workers Compensation Act, and obtain a fire safety certificate and occupancy permit confirming structural load and emergency exit compliance. Complete an emergency response and evacuation plan under the BC Emergency Program Act.
required_dossiers: Environmental screening checklist with office-only operations declaration
Technical Safety BC certification for fire alarm/suppression systems (if installed)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the EAO screens the project in as requiring an exemption letter, submit a short project description for a written 'not reviewable' determination; for WorkSafeBC, respond to any OHS inspection orders by implementing corrective measures and scheduling re-inspection.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Municipal business licensing office of the applicable British Columbia municipality (e.g., City of Vancouver Business Licence Office) in coordination with Technical Safety BC, WorkSafeBC, and the BC Office of the Fire Commissioner
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Business Licence for Information Technology and Data Processing Services and BC Fire Safety / Occupancy Certificate; no separate CRTC or broadcast licensing is required for the real-time video match app at the formation stage

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Assessment Office (EAO), BC Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Not a reviewable project under the Environmental Assessment Act (SBC 2018, c. 35); office and software operations generate no reportable discharge, therefore no Environmental Management Act waste discharge permit is required unless the company operates regulated equipment or discharges beyond domestic sewage
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater discharge; domestic sewage only and must comply with applicable municipal sewer use by-laws (e.g., Metro Vancouver Trunk Sewer and Drainage bylaws). No significant VOC emissions from office activities; HVAC refrigerants and any ozone-depleting substances must comply with the BC Ozone Depleting Substances and Other Halocarbons Regulation (BC Reg. 394/93) and federal ODS Regulations (SOR/2016-137). E-waste and batteries must be handled in accordance with the BC Hazardous Waste Regulation (BC Reg. 63/88) and the Recycling Regulation (BC Reg. 449/2004)

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification and occupancy permit under the BC Fire Code and BC Building Code issued by the local fire authority; structural load inspection for the leased office; building emergency and evacuation plan under the Emergency Program Act (RSBC 1996, c. 111); WorkSafeBC workplace registration and compliance with occupational health and safety standards under the Workers Compensation Act (RSBC 1996, c. 492); electrical and fire alarm system certification by Technical Safety BC where installed

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) — federal income tax, GST/HST, and Business Number (BN) administration. Portal: CRA My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/digital-services-businesses/business-account.html); Business Registration Online (BRO) (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/businesses/topics/registering-your-business/register-business-online.html). Provincial: BC Ministry of Finance for Provincial Sales Tax via eTaxBC (https://etax.gov.bc.ca).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 — Incorporate as a BC Business Corporation (BC Registry/Companies Online) or federal CBCA corporation extra-provincially registered in BC; obtain corporate registry ID. Step 2 — Apply to CRA for the 9-digit Business Number (BN) with corporate income tax (RC) program account via BRO, normally within 90 days of commencing Canadian business; the BN is the statutory TIN (no separate VAT ID exists). Step 3 — Register for GST/HST (RT account) online or by Form RC1; non-residents use the simplified non-resident registration process. Step 4 — Register for BC PST via eTaxBC if taxable goods/services are supplied in BC (including digital products effective July 1, 2025). Step 5 — Maintain a Canadian records address and, where lacking Canadian physical presence, appoint an authorised CRA representative under 'Represent a Client'.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A Canadian Business Corporation is resident under paragraph 250(4)(a) of the Income Tax Act and taxed on worldwide income; no pass-through is available. CCPC status (federal 9% + BC 2% small business deduction on first CAD 500,000 active business income) requires Canadian-resident control; with non-resident ownership permitted, the general rates (federal 15% + BC 12% ≈ 27%) apply. Territorial_Scope: worldwide taxation of the Canadian-resident corporation with foreign tax credits. Tax_Exempt_Zone: none in Canada/BC.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no check-the-box regime. Available elections: (i) GST/HST subsection 156(2) election among closely related corporations for nil-consideration cross-supplies; (ii) GST/HST Quick Method election for small suppliers; (iii) Income Tax Act section 216 election for non-resident recipients to report net Canadian rental income; (iv) section 217 election for non-resident pension income; (v) subsection 256(9) joint election to remove associated-corporation designation where control is by a related person. Hybrid mismatch: mandatory deduction-denial rules (ITA ss. 18.2–18.4) apply non-electively; foreign 'check-the-box' classifications are not recognised — CRA uses functional equivalence.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST) — federal VAT at 5% in British Columbia (BC is not an HST-participating province); plus separate BC Provincial Sales Tax (PST) at 7% administered by the BC Ministry of Finance.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 (annual worldwide taxable supplies; small-supplier threshold, ETA s. 148). For non-resident suppliers of specified digital services, the threshold is measured only against taxable supplies to Canadian recipients; simplified non-resident registration requires no Canadian physical presence. BC PST: registration is required upon the first taxable sale; from July 1, 2025, PST expands to digital products, including apps and online services.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, API, or digital stamping regime in Canada/BC. The CRA accepts electronic invoices (PDF, XML, EDI) without format pre-approval. The Pan-Canadian e-Invoicing Framework voluntarily adopts Peppol BIS; Quebec's B2B e-invoicing mandate (2026) does not apply to BC. Supporting records, including PSP settlement data from Apple IAP and Paymentwall, must be retained for six years under ETA s. 286.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating at 0% GST/HST applies to video-matching and social telephony services supplied to a non-resident recipient not registered for GST/HST, provided the service is not performed in respect of real property in Canada or tangible personal property in Canada (ETA Schedule VI, Part V, s. 9). The supplier must retain evidence of non-resident status: executed agreement, billing address, IP/location data, and payment routing through Apple IAP/Paymentwall. Input tax credits on related Canadian inputs remain recoverable; app-store intermediation does not defeat zero-rating where the underlying supply is made to the non-resident end-user.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration / Export Reporting (only for tangible goods; not required for pure digital service exports)
Bill of Lading or equivalent delivery log (Apple IAP / Paymentwall transaction records evidencing supply and delivery)
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank or PSP settlement statement evidencing non-resident payment inflow
Non-resident self-declaration and executed SaaS/end-user agreement confirming recipient status
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess within four years of the original assessment (unlimited for misrepresentation or fraud). Unsubstantiated zero-rating is reassessed at 5% GST on consideration plus compound daily interest (ETA s. 280); penalties include 25% for false statements (ETA s. 285) and criminal liability for evasion under ETA s. 327 (fines up to 250% of tax evaded and imprisonment up to five years). Previously refunded GST/HST may be clawed back. Records must be kept six years (ETA s. 286). Canada imposes no statutory 180-day FX repatriation deadline for service exports; the figure is a commercial benchmark — materially delayed or absent settlement evidence may cause CRA to challenge non-resident status. BC PST may be separately assessed with interest and penalties for unregistered digital-product sales in BC.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Canada maintains no centralized foreign-exchange-control agency; monetary authority is the Bank of Canada, while financial institutions are prudentially regulated by OSFI and AML/CFT supervised by FINTRAC)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility on both capital and current accounts under the Currency Act and Canada's OECD obligations. There are no exchange-control approvals for foreign direct investment, inbound capital injection, or dividend/profit remittance, subject to customary sanctions screening, beneficial-ownership disclosure, and Canadian withholding tax on distributions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no statutory surrender, holding-period, or mandatory conversion obligation on export receipts; proceeds may be freely retained, converted, or disbursed in any currency. Standard tax and cross-border reporting obligations still apply.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium. Offshore digital EMI/e-money institutions are not permitted to operate as depository institutions in Canada without authorization under the Bank Act. Such entities may engage a Canadian bank sponsor or use a registered money-services-business framework, but they must comply with the Retail Payment Activities Act, FINTRAC registration as a money services business, and provincial consumer-protection rules. A purely offshore EMI cannot legally issue bank-level guarantees or hold guaranteed client funds in Canada.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors are not statutorily required to appear in person provided the financial institution applies a compliant two-factor or reliable independent identity verification process under the PCMLTFA and its Risk-Based Approach. In practice, major Canadian banks often require video interviews, notarized corporate resolutions, and occasionally in-branch sign-off for non-resident-controlled or medium/high-risk corporate accounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Fully remote onboarding with non-resident directors and beneficial owners; lack of physical branch footprint.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified certificate of corporate status, certified articles of incorporation, current director/UBO register, notarized passports, bank reference letters from existing financial institutions, board resolution authorizing account opening, and a detailed source-of-wealth statement with supporting contracts and invoices.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business activity classified as real-time video matching / random video chat; elevated exposure to user-generated content and potential unlawful adult content.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Production of platform risk and compliance policies, content-moderation workflow, age-gating verification report, end-user terms of service, privacy policy, third-party AML/sanctions screening program, and periodic independent external audit certificates.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume, low-value micro-transactions from aggregators such as Apple IAP and Paymentwall; difficulty tracing final end users.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Aggregator agreements, merchant settlement statements, payment-rail reconciliation reports, chargeback and fraud monitoring summaries, transaction-screening logic, and documented know-your-customer protocols applied to commercial counterparties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident capital injection expected via SWIFT MT103 from offshore jurisdictions with elevated money-laundering risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-funds for each capital injection, copy of inbound wire instructions and purpose code, supported by audited financial statements, shareholder loan agreements, corporate registers, and tax residency certificates.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border treasury mirroring the parent company in a non-IGA jurisdiction; potential concern about CFC attribution or structuring abuse.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: International corporate structure chart, transfer-pricing documentation, substance and decision-making evidence, management accounting records, tax opinion letter, and statutory filings demonstrating genuine economic activity in British Columbia.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing uses a standard SWIFT MT103 wire from the parent's or beneficial owner's bank to the Canadian entity's operational or capital escrow account held at a Schedule I bank. The wire should carry a clear remittance narrative such as 'Capital Injection / Shareholders' Loan', the beneficiary's full legal name, and the Canadian bank transit and institution numbers. Verification requires source-of-funds evidence, board approval, COR-9 or similar corporate extract, FINTRAC and sanctions screening, and, where applicable, statutory reporting of the intra-group financing and interest or dividend characterization.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade and service disbursements are cleared using SWIFT MT103 payments for international suppliers, and, where physical goods are purchased, via a commercial letter of credit (typically a confirmed or unconfirmed LC) negotiated against transport and invoicing documents. Domestic Canadian-dollar disbursements clear through Payments Canada systems, including LVTS (large-value real-time payments) and ACSS; USD and foreign-currency disbursements settle through the bank's correspondent network and SWIFT. All wires are subject to OFSI/PACMLTFA screening and transactional record-keeping obligations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within two months after the anniversary of incorporation each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The company is placed in arrears and becomes subject to a statutory late-filing penalty; two consecutive missed annual reports permit the Registrar to administratively strike off or dissolve the company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six months after the corporation's fiscal year end; June 30 where the fiscal year ends December 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month for up to 12 months; habitual default may trigger CRA compliance action, reassessments, and director liability assessments.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Three months after the corporation's fiscal year end for annual GST/HST filers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CRA arrears interest and penalties apply to late or omitted GST/HST returns; serious or repeated failures may result in formal demands, enhanced verification audits, and corporate director liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T4 / T4 Summary (Statement of Remuneration Paid)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than the last day of February following the calendar year in which remuneration was paid
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CRA late-filing penalties accrue per day on missing or delinquent T4 slips, subject to prescribed minimums and maximums; continued failures may expose directors to payroll source deduction liabilities.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No automatic audit threshold applies to a private BC business corporation; an independent audit is mandatory only where the company is a reporting issuer under Canadian securities law, where shareholders validly requisition an audit, or where CRA or another regulator requires audited financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for public and reporting issuers; ASPE under CPA Canada Handbook Part II for private BC corporations.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: BC does not require a separate public annual UBO return; the company must maintain a confidential BC transparency register of significant individuals, promptly record share transfers and beneficial ownership changes, and review and confirm the register annually as part of the secretarial audit accompanying the annual report cycle.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: No statutory audit fee is ordinarily incurred for a private BC corporation; a voluntary or regulator-required small-entity audit typically ranges from CAD 10,000 - CAD 25,000 (USD 7,500 - USD 18,500).

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 15% federal + 12% British Columbia provincial = 27% combined general corporate income tax rate (as of 2024/2025; subject to provincial budget changes)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general federal tax holiday; small business deduction (SBD) reduces federal rate to 9% on first CAD 500,000 of active business income for Canadian-controlled private corporations (CCPCs), with corresponding BC small business deduction to 2% (combined ~11%). Non-CCPCs and non-resident corporations generally do not qualify. Deductions include arm's-length interest, R&D expenses, and accelerated capital cost allowance.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (T2) filed through the Canada Revenue Agency's (CRA) E-file / NETFILE for corporations (GST/HST included on same return). Provincial: BC Corporate Tax Return (BC T2) integrated with the federal T2; filed via e-File through approved software or transmitted electronically to CRA and BC Ministry of Finance.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Six months after the corporation's fiscal year-end. For a fiscal year ending December 31, deadline is June 30. Payments of federal and provincial tax instalments are due quarterly for corporations exceeding thresholds; balance due 2 months after year-end for CCPCs, 3 months for non-CCPCs (certain loss offsets may extend).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business income or loss from the video chat app operations (determined under generally accepted accounting principles, adjusted for tax purposes, including Canadian source revenues from in-app purchases and subscription fees).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Canadian-source business income attributable to the Canadian permanent establishment (PE), if the corporation is a non-resident. If no PE, file under Part IX.1 of the T2 or the simplified Form T2NR, unless treaty protection applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total taxable income after deductions (loss carryforwards, capital gains allowance, intercompany adjustments).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents compute taxable income based on Canadian-source income deemed attributable to a PE; transfer pricing adjustments must be reflected.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal and provincial income tax payable after applying combined rates, tax credits (e.g., digital GST/HST input tax credits related to platform costs) and foreign tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Part XIV non-resident surtax (25% on certain Canadian-source payments) may apply unless reduced by treaty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transfer pricing disclosure: aggregate value of transactions with non-arm's length non-residents (e.g., licensing of video matching software from parent, royalties for IP, shared service costs).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mandatory for all non-arm's length cross-border transactions exceeding CAD 1 million gross; Schedule 88 must be completed even if no allocation to a Canadian PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: BC provincial tax computation using BC taxable income and BC statutory rates (large corporation tax / minimum tax applicable if taxable capital exceeds CAD 10 million).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate income to BC if the corporation carries on business through a permanent establishment in BC.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of unpaid tax for return filed late plus 1% per full month (up to 12 months). If assessed gross negligence (knowingly or under circumstances of gross negligence), penalty is 50% of the understatement (federal and provincial combined). Daily interest accrues on late and unpaid balances at CRA prescribed rate (currently 9% for corporations for 2025 Q1, compounded daily). Provincial interest similarly applied. Failing to file electronically when required results in CAD 500 to CAD 7,500 penalty.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% (Part XIII) on dividends paid to non-resident shareholders, unless reduced by treaty (e.g., Canada–US treaty reduces to 5% on substantial holdings or 15% otherwise; Canada–China treaty 10% on 10%+ holding; UK/Ireland treaties 15%/5%).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke tax treaty relief, the beneficial owner of the dividend must submit Form NR301 (or NR302 for partnership), a valid Certificate of Residence (TRC) issued by the home jurisdiction tax authority, and complete a treaty-based waiver (e.g., Canada's Form NR301-S). Ensure the entity has economic substance in the home jurisdiction; CRA may require a TRC covering the specific dividend payment year. Apply before or at the time of payment; retroactive treaty application is possible through Form T1-T or amended NR4 filings, subject to a 3-year statutory limitation period. Use of a shell company without substance will be denied treaty benefits under the Principal Purpose Test (PPT) or Limitation on Benefits (LOB) clauses.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalty withholding tax: statutory 25% (Part XIII) on payments for use of IP, with treaty rates commonly 0%–10% (US 0%, China 10%, UK/NL 10%, Ireland 10%). Interest withholding tax: statutory 25% (Part XIII), treaty rates typically 0%–15% (US 15% or 0% for arm's length; China 10%; UK 10%). Withholding must be remitted to CRA by the 15th day of the month following the payment; failure to withhold renders the payer liable for the gross amount plus penalties.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory contemporaneous documentation (Master File and Local File) must be prepared if the aggregate gross value of specified transactions with non-residents exceeds CAD 1,000,000 for a fiscal year (Schedule 88 threshold). No statutory service fee threshold for documentation; only threshold is CAD 1 million. A Master File is required if the multinational group's Canadian revenue or assets exceed CAD 50M, or if total group revenue exceeds CAD 750M and cross-border transactions exceed CAD 1M. Country-by-Country reporting applies to groups with consolidated revenue ≥ EUR 750M / CAD 1.1B.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not have a general ESR; however, treaty benefit provisions (PPT, LOB), GAAR (General Anti-Abuse Rule under s.245 of the Income Tax Act), and CRA's anti-avoidance doctrine scrutinize entities lacking substance. A foreign parent company claiming treaty relief must demonstrate real substantive business presence, decision-making, and risk management in its residence state. Dividend stripping rules (s.55) deny capital dividend treatment where a transaction is essentially to avoid tax. Canada's Place of Effective Management (POEM) doctrine and the Authorized OECD Approach (AOA) may recharacterize profits if a Canadian corporation is managed from abroad.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting revenue from Canadian app users, underreporting in-app purchases, or using nominee shareholders to conceal the beneficial owner and avoid Canadian taxation. Failing to report foreign bank accounts or hiding intercompany revenue transfers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal prosecution under s.239 of the Income Tax Act: fines of up to 200% of the tax evaded or up to CAD 100,000, imprisonment up to 5 years (federal). Civil penalties: 50% gross negligence penalty, 100% penalty for false statements or omission (s.163), plus accumulated interest. BC Provincial: similar penalties under BC Income Tax Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers may be personally liable under s.227.1 for unpaid corporate withholdings (e.g., employee source deductions, GST/HST). Personal liability can also attach for prosecutions if the director was willfully blind or actively participated. Prison sentences of up to 5 years; travel bans can be imposed under criminal justice procedures; civil restitution to CRA may include seizure of personal assets and bank accounts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: A non-resident holding company with no office, staff, or operational substance in its claimed residence, used solely to receive Canadian dividends or royalties at reduced treaty rates. Canadian resident corporation managed entirely from abroad without Canadian substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits under GAAR ss.245(2) and treaty PPT/LOB clauses. CRA may recharacterize dividends as deemed taxable dividends or royalties under s.212, apply 25% Part XIII withholding, charge interest and penalties of 50% for reckless omission, and impose double taxation risk.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign false returns or cause the corporation to misrepresent its structure may be subject to civil assessments under joint and several liability (s.221.1), and under the Criminal Code for fraudulent manipulation of stock exchange or tax evasion (s.380). Personal assets may be frozen; travel bans where criminal prosecution is initiated.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a random video chat app used for cross-border payments (Apple IAP, Paymentwall) without registering as a Money Service Business (MSB) or fulfilling FINTRAC reporting obligations for large virtual currency transactions, suspicious transactions, or suspicious attempted transactions. Allowing the platform to be used for illicit financial flows or failing to maintain beneficial ownership records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: FINTRAC administrative monetary penalties up to CAD 1,000,000 for non-compliant MSBs (per violation); failure to report suspicious transactions up to CAD 1,000,000. Criminal penalties for knowingly laundering proceeds of crime under Criminal Code s.462.31: imprisonment up to 10 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be personally prosecuted if they knew or ought to have known of the laundering activity; civil penalties and orders to disgorge profits; travel bans may be imposed by court as a bail condition. Personal criminal liability includes imprisonment up to 5 years (money laundering) or 10 years (organized crime).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends to a non-resident parent corporation without withholding 25% (or treaty reduced rate) and without obtaining a valid TRC, or executing a series of transactions to strip corporate surplus as capital gains (s.55) to avoid dividend withholding.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Payer is personally liable for unwithheld tax under s.215(4); penalty of 10% if not withheld, and director liability under s.227.1. GAAR recharacterization results in deemed dividends with Part XIII tax, plus interest and penalties. Gross negligence penalties (50%) if intentional.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed authorization for payment without proper withholding become jointly and severally liable for the unremitted tax and can be pursued for personal assets; criminal negligence can lead to imprisonment up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare contemporaneous documentation or making a transfer pricing adjustment in excess of CAD 100,000 in a single year, where a transaction between related parties (e.g., licensing of video matching IP to a Canadian subsidiary at a non-arm's length royalty) is not at arm's length.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer pricing penalty under s.247(3): 10% of the gross understated income (or overstated loss) for each adjustment, in addition to any other Canadian tax assessed. No cap under Canadian law. For repeated or egregious cases, CRA may apply negligence penalties (50%).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve non-arm's length transactions without independent functional analysis may face civil liability for resulting corporate tax shortfalls if they acted in bad faith; sexual? No; but personal liability for unreported withholdings remains. In severe cases, criminal prosecution for making false statements (s.380) can lead to imprisonment up to 5 years.
